locator: §3.5, 'Stevenson (1944) begins his book by distinguishing the kind of disagreement in play when two people disagree in their ordinary beliefs from “disagreements in attitude” which involve conative clash.'
interpretation: Stevenson distinguishes disagreement in belief from 'disagreements in attitude', a conative clash, holds that moral disagreements involve both, and uses this to motivate his emotivism. Read as the emotivist's replacement answer to Q-MORAL-DISAGREEMENT: the distinctively moral part of a disagreement is a clash of attitudes, not a contradiction. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
